note: Chat composer drafts: a sequence of composer actions and the draft the store must hold afterwards. `draft` is null when no row should exist -- an empty draft and no draft are different states, and rule 2 is the difference. `type` sets the composer text absolutely; `leave` is the screen going away, which flushes. Text is stored verbatim, including whitespace; trimming happens at submit only. Behavior parity, not a computation with an external reference. The failed-send case is deliberately absent: it is the one behaviour the two platforms deliberately differ on.

vectors.name: verbatim-trailing-space
vectors.note: Rule 1. The trailing space is mid-sentence, not noise: trimming belongs at submit, which is where both apps already do it.

vectors.name: verbatim-leading-space
vectors.note: Rule 1 again, on the way back out: restore does not trim either.

vectors.name: whitespace-only-is-no-draft
vectors.note: Rule 2. Trims to empty with no reply target, so the row is removed rather than stored as whitespace.

vectors.name: cleared-after-typing-is-no-draft
vectors.note: Rule 2's actual failure mode: without the delete, a chat typed in once and cleared restores an empty draft for ever.

vectors.name: bare-reply-target-is-a-draft
vectors.note: Rule 3. Aiming a reply and walking away is intent worth keeping, and dropping it is the wrong-context send this feature exists to prevent.

vectors.name: reply-target-with-text
vectors.note: The ordinary case: both halves come back together.

vectors.name: whitespace-with-reply-target-is-a-draft
vectors.note: Rule 2 needs BOTH halves empty. The strip is still aimed, so the row stays -- and rule 1 still stores the whitespace verbatim.

vectors.name: reply-target-cleared-leaves-the-text
vectors.note: Dismissing the strip is not clearing the message.

vectors.name: send-clears
vectors.note: Rule 4. The text lives in the pending message the moment the field clears; a draft as well would duplicate it.

vectors.name: send-clears-the-reply-target-too
vectors.note: Rule 4 covers the whole draft, not just its text.

vectors.name: edit-persists-the-stash
vectors.note: Rule 5. What is saved is the new-message draft the edit displaced, never the edit body -- leaving mid-edit must not overwrite your words with someone else's message.

vectors.name: edit-cancelled-restores-the-stash
vectors.note: Same answer by the path both apps already implement: cancelling an edit puts the stashed draft back.

vectors.name: edit-with-nothing-stashed-is-no-draft
vectors.note: Rule 5 with an empty composer: the edit displaced nothing, so there is nothing to persist.
